title: Mariska Hargitay Just Won Two Emmys in One Night — Here's the Story Behind Them
metaDescription: Mariska Hargitay walked away from the 2026 Emmys with two statuettes for 'My Mom Jayne.' Here's what she won for, and why it means more than most awards.
html:
Most people walk into an awards show hoping for one trophy. Mariska Hargitay walked out of the 2026 Emmy Awards with two — and neither of them was for the role that made her famous.

During the Creative Arts portion of this year's ceremony, Hargitay picked up two Emmy statuettes for her work on "My Mom Jayne," the HBO documentary she wrote, directed, and starred in about her late mother, screen icon Jayne Mansfield. The film premiered at the 2025 Cannes and Tribeca festivals before debuting on HBO on June 27, and it marks Hargitay's first major directing credit after nearly three decades in front of the camera on "Law & Order: SVU."

The ceremony itself was a big night across the board. "Hacks," "Widow's Bay," and "The Pitt" dominated the nominations field, with guest-acting trophies going to Betty Gilpin for "Widow's Bay," Ernest Harden Jr. for "The Pitt," and Shailene Woodley for "Paradise." In a more bittersweet moment, Rob Reiner was honored posthumously with Outstanding Guest Actor in a Comedy Series for his final work on "The Bear."

But it's Hargitay's win that's generating the most conversation online — not because of the category, but because of what the film represents. Mansfield, a 1950s and '60s Hollywood sex symbol, died in a car accident in 1967 when Hargitay was three years old. "My Mom Jayne" follows Hargitay's decades-long attempt to understand who her mother really was, beyond the pin-up image that outlived her.

For a performer best known for playing a detective who gives other people's trauma a voice, turning the camera toward her own family history — and getting rewarded for it on television's biggest night — is the kind of full-circle moment awards shows rarely produce on purpose.
